default_selection.eras: auto (by the run's start_at: < 2023-11-01 pre_red_sea_crisis; 2023-11-01 .. 2026-06-30 red_sea_diversion; from 2026-07-01 red_sea_diversion + partial_suez_return_2026)

policy.frequency: null unless the source states it; never invented
policy.leg_rule: A leg is two consecutive MAPPED calls with no dropped call between them. The loop closes (last call to first) only where the source prints a chokepoint marker after the last call. A call that repeats the previous call makes no leg. Entries with a sequence_caveat build no leg between the two sides of the Suez basin.
policy.unstated_routing_policy: Entries whose routing basis is unstated, article_text_indirect or conflicting_sources (and the one article_text entry that names no chokepoint) say nothing positive about a chokepoint. They are kept in the sidecar for audit and excluded by default; include_unstated: true admits them (their legs are then local legs with no stated chokepoint).
policy.unverified_policy: The 21 entries whose excerpt could only be fetched through WebFetch's extractor (Ocean Alliance Day 9, Apr 2025, 17 entries; Day 3, 2019, 4 entries) carry flag webfetch_not_machine_verified. They cannot be diffed against the saved page text, so they are EXCLUDED from every default selection and enter a run only when the body says include_unverified: true (journaled).
policy.via_rule: A chokepoint is on a leg when the source prints its marker after the leg's origin call (SOURCED, positioned); when the source states the routing for the whole service or the era default applies, it is on the legs that cross the basin by zone (MODELLED placement, graph_services.zones); Bab el-Mandeb is added to a Suez leg whose eastern end lies outside the Red Sea (MODELLED, geographic necessity: no other water connection).

provenance.licensing: port sequences are facts; the pages are copyrighted trade press and carrier releases. Only sequences and a first-25-word excerpt are stored. Entries are announcements, not proof of sailed routes.
